source.title: Beyond Local Sharpness: Communication-Efficient Global Sharpness-aware Minimization for Federated Learning
source.authors: Debora Caldarola; Pietro Cagnasso; Barbara Caputo; Marco Ciccone

record.tranche_reason: Tests sharpness and held-out classification performance in heterogeneous federated learning, a new setting relative to the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own test accuracies and sharpness measures for federated methods. It does not test random-label memorization, the listed optimizer/batch-size/regularization comparisons, or magnitude-aware sharpness tracking the train-test gap. Cited findings from prior work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses the sharpness–generalization rationale to develop a federated optimizer and evaluates its performance. Its Hessian eigenvalues and loss visualizations do not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, train–test error gaps, or ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that heterogeneity creates local–global geometry discrepancies, and that FedGloSS combines server-side SAM, past pseudo-gradients and ADMM to improve global flatness, accuracy and communication efficiency. They also attribute improved ADMM stability to SAM preventing parameter explosion.
record.recipe_differences: Federated training with server-side SAM and ADMM consistency; evaluated against federated methods rather than the listed centralized recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Data heterogeneity, architecture, local optimizer, and server-side ρs affect reported accuracy or sharpness outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: FedGloSS improves benchmark accuracy and generally lowers maximum Hessian eigenvalues relative to the compared federated methods. Increasing its server perturbation radius can lower eigenvalues while reducing accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Server-side sharpness-aware optimization can improve heterogeneous federated image classification, but lower maximum Hessian eigenvalues do not invariably imply higher test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Client models can occupy flat local loss regions while having substantially sharper geometry on the global dataset.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local flatness does not ensure global flatness in heterogeneous federated learning.

record.problems: The experiments concern federated learning and do not measure the train-test gap or the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7. Some sharpness and loss-landscape comparisons are figure-based; the reported tables provide maximum Hessian eigenvalues and accuracy, not direct perturbation tolerance or a causal test of sharpness-generalization correlation.
record.rows_left_out: Other method-by-method benchmark values and appendix configurations were not extracted; the selected rows capture the central accuracy comparison, a sharpness comparator, and an explicitly described sensitivity result. Tables 3, 9, and Appendix Figure 20 contain further values.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove them.
Dropout effects and interactions with dataset size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness tracking train–test error gaps among similarly fitted networks, including comparisons with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: A new federated setting does not warrant T3 when the measured constructs do not match any listed version. Local–global sharpness discrepancies and exceptions to a Hessian-eigenvalue–accuracy association do not challenge V7's distinct measure and outcome.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond the interpolation threshold and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under tuning choices.
Large-batch generalization gap and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness tracking the train-test gap; the study reports maximum Hessian eigenvalues and test accuracy in federated learning, not the version's measure or gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: CNN

rows.measure: test accuracy (%) and maximum Hessian eigenvalue λ1
rows.note: These are federated benchmark results; the measures do not establish any listed version.
rows.check: This combines multiple datasets, optimizers, methods and measures and should be split. Table 3 reports accuracy, not Hessian eigenvalues; those are in Table 9 and Figure 7. The baseline labeled FedAvg with SAM is FedSAM. The reported accuracy values otherwise match Table 3. These are method-performance comparisons, not evidence for a listed version.

rows.subject: FedSAM
rows.operation_detail: Reported maximum Hessian eigenvalues for comparison with FedGloSS.
rows.note: Sharpness values are not the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7.
rows.check: The eigenvalues match Table 9, but the two heterogeneity conditions should be separate rows. Maximum Hessian eigenvalues alone cannot establish V7.

rows.subject: FedGloSS
rows.operation_detail: Measured test accuracy and maximum Hessian eigenvalue while varying server-side SAM neighborhood size.
rows.measure: accuracy (%) and maximum Hessian eigenvalue λ1
rows.value: The text states smaller ρs usually leads to the best accuracy; larger ρs leads to lower eigenvalues with minimum loss in accuracy. Figure values: figure only.
rows.note: The text describes the direction of changes; exact plotted values are not assigned here.
rows.check: Replace partial: the measures cannot determine any listed version's effect. Figure 20b reports lower Hessian eigenvalues with larger server perturbation radius and some loss of accuracy. The supplied figure text includes numerical annotations, so describing all values as figure-only is incomplete. Separate accuracy and eigenvalue results by radius.
